args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression and look into why it was promoted despite the unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions, and the health checks are passing again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it. The service reports healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and has paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the checks afterward. It also notes the test version of v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging before it reached production. Follow-ups are to find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and why it was released despite failing in staging.

Change-manager approval wasn't needed: v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
